[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning Strategies in Deep Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Transfer learning is a machine learning technique where a model developed for a task is reused as the starting point for a model on a second task. In deep learning, this typically involves taking a neural network pretrained on a massive dataset like ImageNet and adapting it to a custom, domain-specific dataset with limited samples."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Use Transfer Learning?"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reduced Training Time: Pretrained models have already learned rich feature representations, drastically cutting down convergence time."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Higher Performance: Models often achieve superior accuracy on smaller target datasets compared to training from scratch."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Efficiency: Solves the problem of scarcity by leveraging knowledge distilled from millions of general-purpose data points."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Fine-Tuning Strategies"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Depending on the size of your dataset and its similarity to the original training domain, you can choose from several adaptation strategies:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Feature Extraction (Frozen Backbone): Freeze all layers of the pretrained model except the final classification head. Train only the new classifier on your target data."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Partial Fine-Tuning: Freeze the early layers (which capture low-level features like edges and textures) and unfreeze the deeper layers to adapt high-level semantic representations."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Full Fine-Tuning: Unfreeze the entire network and train all weights using a very small learning rate to avoid catastrophic forgetting."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementation Example using PyTorch"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical implementation of loading a pretrained ResNet18 model, freezing its feature extractor, and replacing the final classification layer for a custom 10-class problem."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torchvision.models as models

# Load pretrained ResNet18
weights = models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT
model = models.resnet18(weights=weights)

# Freeze all parameter gradients
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# Replace the final fully connected layer for 10 output classes
num_features = model.fc.in_features
model.fc = nn.Linear(num_features, 10)

# Only the new layer parameters have requires_grad=True by default
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.fc.parameters(), lr=0.001)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Fine-Tuning"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use a Smaller Learning Rate: Pretrained weights are already optimal; a large learning rate will destroy learned representations."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Discriminative Learning Rates: Apply lower learning rates to earlier layers and higher learning rates to newly added layers."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gradual Unfreezing: Train the classification head first, then unfreeze layers block by block from top to bottom."}]
